summary: Restoration is the core of Mauritania’s pledges: restore 50,000 ha of degraded ecosystems and 100,000 ha overall, reforest 31,686 ha of village woodlots, and expand annual interventions including 4,000 ha/year of unconditional reforestation, 5,000 ha/year of assisted forest regeneration, and a potential additional 10,000 ha/year through regional programmes. Other plans cover 5,332 ha of dune stabilization, 500 ha of mangroves and 2,075 ha of land exclusion. Conservation targets 1,126 km² of marine protected areas, 150,000 ha of aerial seeding, 20 classified forests, 10 wetlands and protection of coastal and dune systems. Agriculture includes 6,000 ha of organic/agroecology, 10,000 ha/year of cover crops, 6,000 ha of no-till farming by 2030, and 20,000 ha of pastoral reserves. The village-woodlot programme alone equals about 26.7% of current forest cover, while organic/agroecology covers about 0.3% of current agricultural land.
